newsitem.title: CANADA: United Grain shares rise on deal.
newsitem.headline: United Grain shares rise on deal.

text.p: United Grain Growers Ltd shares hit a record high of $16 in early, heavy trade on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Thursday's news of a C$113 million deal with Archer Daniels Midland Co, analysts said.

"UGG's stock's up on the ADM deal. The reason it's down from C$16 a share is they're testing the old highs, it's on technicals, there's no fundamental reason for it to be down," ScotiaMcLeod commodities and equities analyst Rob Gigiel said.
UGG stock was up C$0.60 to $15 a share at 1120 EDT after going as high as C$16, the share price set in the deal with ADM Thursday, with 378,494 shares changing hands.

UGG shares closed Wednesday at C$14.40 each, C$0.20 below the previous high of C$14.60. Trading in UGG was halted on the TSE and Winnipeg Stock Exchange Thursday pending the ADM announcement and resumed earlier on Friday.
UGG's president, chief executive and chief financial officers were not immediately available for comment as they met staff to explain the details of the ADM deal.
UGG is Canada's second largest grain handler while ADM is one of the world's largest food processors.
